And the hard part is rarely the idea.

But I think the harder part is really the selection and the system.

Not every employee should be posting.

The people who will actually move the needle are usually a mix of those who already have some audience.

And a smaller group of operators who are willing to be consistent.

The mistake would be either forcing everyone to post, which eventually creates low-quality noise and resentment,

or leaving it completely unstructured, where only the most outgoing people keep going while everyone else drops off after a few weeks

In practice, starting with 3–5 people who are already close to customers or have something specific and useful to say might be ideal

Give them clear lanes, topics, proof points and light support

Then measure whether their content is actually creating conversations and inbound interest, not just impressions
